question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the constant multiple rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{4})) \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{4}))\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the product and the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{4})) & ={x}^{2}\cdot (\frac{∂}{∂y}(y)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{4})+y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{4})) \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot (1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{4})+y\cdot \frac{1}{{y}^{4}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{4})) \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{4})+\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}\cdot (4{y}^{3}))) \\  & ={x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{4})+4)\end{aligned}
$$
